project_requirements.title: What the call wants
project_requirements.question: What must the project address, develop and achieve?

cards.title: Central object
cards.question: What is the principal thing the project must develop?
cards.answer: Demonstrate new or improved storage technology integrated into infrastructure retrofits.
cards.sources: Integrated Approaches for Retrofitting Infrastructures with Innovative Energy Storage Technologies · Topic description, Scope

cards.title: Scope
cards.question: Which activities fall within the funding opportunity's scope?
cards.answer: Proposals should address storage performance, circularity and socioeconomic and environmental sustainability.
cards.sources: Integrated Approaches for Retrofitting Infrastructures with Innovative Energy Storage Technologies · Topic description, Scope

cards.title: Problem
cards.question: What type of problem or need must justify the project, and where must it originate?
cards.answer: The energy system needs additional flexible storage capacity that makes productive use of obsolete infrastructure.
cards.sources: Integrated Approaches for Retrofitting Infrastructures with Innovative Energy Storage Technologies · Topic description, Expected Outcome and Scope

cards.title: Deliverables
cards.question: Which concrete outputs must the project produce?
cards.answer: Develop the storage retrofit demonstration and its essential monitoring deliverables. The standard form also requires data-management and dissemination/exploitation plans within six months.
cards.sources:
Integrated Approaches for Retrofitting Infrastructures with Innovative Energy Storage Technologies · Topic description, Scope
Standard application form, HE RIA and IA, Part B, version 5.1 · Part B p. 17 of 23 · Table 3.1c: List of Deliverables

cards.title: Impact
cards.question: Which wider system outcomes and impacts must the project support?
cards.answer: Results are expected to improve energy security, storage sustainability and circularity, and the economic viability of storage through infrastructure reuse.
cards.sources: Integrated Approaches for Retrofitting Infrastructures with Innovative Energy Storage Technologies · Topic description, Expected Outcome

cards.title: After the project
cards.question: How must the result be replicated, taken up and kept in use after the project?
cards.answer: Selected projects are expected to participate actively in BRIDGE, the cooperation initiative for European energy projects. The proposal must include exploitation, dissemination and communication planning.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · p. 180 · Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 4 · Admissibility

cards.title: Number of partners
cards.question: What is the permitted or required consortium size?
cards.answer: The consortium must include at least three independent beneficiaries.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 13 · Consortium composition

cards.title: Partner composition
cards.question: Which types of partners must the consortium include?
cards.answer: The beneficiaries must come from three different countries: one EU Member State and two other Member States or associated countries.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 13 · Consortium composition

cards.title: Distribution of work
cards.question: How must work and budget be distributed among partners?

cards.title: Coordinator
cards.question: What type of organisation may or must act as lead applicant?
cards.answer: The beneficiaries choose a coordinator from their consortium to manage the storage demonstration and represent them before the funder.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 36 · Coordinator

project_requirements.title: TenneT's position
project_requirements.question: What is TenneT's position within the consortium?

cards.title: Coordinate
cards.question: Can TenneT apply or coordinate, and under which conditions?

cards.title: Participate
cards.question: Can TenneT take part without receiving funding?
cards.answer: TenneT may take part without receiving funding: unfunded associated participation is permitted.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 4–5, 11, 13 · Entities eligible to participate; Entities eligible for funding; Consortium composition

cards.title: Receive funding
cards.question: Can TenneT receive funding, and which funding rate or cost rules apply?
cards.answer: TenneT TSO B.V. can join as a funded Dutch beneficiary, subject to the eligibility and consortium conditions. TenneT’s company costs can receive up to 70% support through the lump-sum calculation. It must cover the remainder under the central Horizon rules.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 4–5, 11, 13 · Entities eligible to participate; Entities eligible for funding; Consortium composition
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 31–32 · Form of grant, funding rate and maximum grant amount

cards.title: TenneT's likely contribution
cards.question: What contribution would make TenneT credible and useful within the project?
cards.answer: TenneT could help define grid-integration requirements and assess the flexibility delivered by a storage retrofit. This interpretation follows the topic’s grid-flexibility objective and TenneT’s experience with flexible storage connections.
cards.sources: Integrated Approaches for Retrofitting Infrastructures with Innovative Energy Storage Technologies · Topic description, Scope

project_requirements.title: Innovation
project_requirements.question: What type of innovation must the project develop?

cards.title: Innovation threshold
cards.question: Must the project produce genuinely new knowledge or technology, or may it integrate and apply existing solutions?

cards.title: Innovation object
cards.question: In what must the project innovate?

cards.title: Development stages
cards.question: Which development stages must the project cover?

cards.title: Maturity
cards.question: Which maturity level is expected at the start and end of the project?
cards.answer: Activities may start at any TRL and are expected to reach TRL 6–8 by project end.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · p. 179 · Technology Readiness Level

project_requirements.title: Work
project_requirements.question: Which activities or work structure must the project cover?

cards.title: Demonstration
cards.question: Where and under which conditions must the solution be demonstrated?
cards.answer: Use obsolete or outdated infrastructure, such as decommissioned power plants, old hydropower facilities, former industrial sites or coal mines, for the storage demonstration.
cards.sources: Integrated Approaches for Retrofitting Infrastructures with Innovative Energy Storage Technologies · Topic description, Scope

cards.title: Integration
cards.question: How must the activities fit together and with existing systems?

cards.title: Evidence
cards.question: What must the demonstration prove?

cards.title: User participation
cards.question: How must users take part in the project?

cards.title: Safety and cybersecurity
cards.question: Which safety, cybersecurity or data requirements must the project meet?
cards.answer: Proposals should incorporate security by design. Participants must provide necessary background access; the funder does not acquire ownership of project results. Access supporting scientific publications must safeguard legitimate constraints.
cards.sources:
Integrated Approaches for Retrofitting Infrastructures with Innovative Energy Storage Technologies · Topic description, Scope
EU Lump Sum Model Grant Agreement · p. 31 · Articles 16.1–16.2
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 34 · Open science - additional practices, validation of scientific publications

funding_timing_submission.title: Funding
funding_timing_submission.question: How much funding can the project receive?

cards.title: Funding envelope
cards.answer:
The topic provides EUR 22.5 million, with three grants indicated.
- Grant request: around EUR 7.5 million per project; different requests remain eligible.
- Funding form: lump sum.
cards.sources:
Integrated Approaches for Retrofitting Infrastructures with Innovative Energy Storage Technologies · General information; Budget overview
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 178–179 · Specific conditions

cards.title: Funding rate and co-financing
cards.answer:
Rates are applied when calculating each participant’s lump-sum share.
- Companies: maximum 70%; at least 30% own contribution.
- Non-profit legal entities: up to 100%; no minimum own contribution at that rate.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 31–32 · Form of grant, funding rate and maximum grant amount

cards.title: Budget constraints
cards.answer:
Budget estimates must correspond to eligible costs of the planned retrofit work.
- Eligible costs: personnel, subcontracting and purchases.
- Overheads and VAT: indirect costs use 25% of the eligible base, excluding subcontracting and other specified categories.
- Subcontracting or equipment: justify subcontracting; normally estimate equipment depreciation, not the full purchase price.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 27, 32 · Submission; Budget categories and cost eligibility rules
Lump Sum Funding: What Do I Need to Know?, version 3.0 · slides 34, 36 · Subcontracting costs; Depreciation costs list

cards.title: Cash flow and financial exposure
cards.answer:
Work-package completion controls payment, so unfinished retrofit work can delay cash receipts.
- Payment model: pre-financing, then payments for completed and accepted work packages; partial final payment can apply.
- Retention or guarantee: 5–8% of the maximum grant is deducted for the mutual insurance mechanism.
- Financial reporting or audit: retain implementation evidence; no actual-cost reporting.
cards.sources:
Lump Sum Funding: What Do I Need to Know?, version 3.0 · slides 17–22 · Payment schedule; Reporting and payment; Acceptance of work packages; Keeping records
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 33 · Reporting & payment arrangements

funding_timing_submission.title: Timing
funding_timing_submission.question: What timing should the proposal submission and project follow?

cards.title: Application route
cards.answer:
Submit one full proposal electronically through the Funding & Tenders Portal.
- Single stage — Full proposal: 2027-12-01, 17:00 Brussels time; the lump-sum application limit is 45 pages.
- Opening: planned for 2027-08-04.
cards.sources:
Integrated Approaches for Retrofitting Infrastructures with Innovative Energy Storage Technologies · General information
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 4 · Page limits

cards.title: Project window
cards.answer:
The grant agreement will set the retrofit project’s start and duration.
- Required start: normally after grant signature; an earlier start requires exceptional, justified approval.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 30–31 · Starting date & project duration

cards.title: Decision and contracting
cards.answer:
Evaluation and contracting follow an indicative schedule from the full-proposal deadline.
- Expected invitation or assessment result: around five months after submission closes.
- Grant agreement: around eight months after submission closes.
- Conditions before starting: beneficiaries must conclude a written consortium agreement.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 30, 36 · Indicative timetable for evaluation and for signature of the grant agreement; Consortium agreement

funding_timing_submission.title: Application
funding_timing_submission.question: Mandatory information to include in the application

cards.title: Mandatory submission package — pass/fail
cards.answer:
Use the forms issued in this topic’s submission system.
- Application form: online Part A and technical Part B PDF.
- Budget: detailed estimates by participant, work package and cost category; upload the Excel annex as .xlsx or .xls.
- Partner documents: coordinator mandate confirmation; declarations of honour before grant signature.
- Registration: each participant needs a PIC.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 27, 36 · Submission; Registration
Lump Sum Funding: What Do I Need to Know?, version 3.0 · slides 6–7, 40 · Writing a lump sum proposal; Uploading the Excel file

cards.title: Evaluation and selection — scored or ranked
cards.answer:
Proposals are ranked on excellence, impact and implementation.
- Thresholds: at least 3/5 per criterion and 10/15 overall.
- Weighting: impact receives a 1.5 multiplier for ranking.
- Ranking rules: ties first favour uncovered topic aspects, then impact and excellence, with further diversity criteria.
- Budget assessment: unreasonable estimates can reduce the lump sum; serious budget defects can lower implementation scores.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 23, 26, 28 · Award criteria; Scores and weighting; Evaluation procedure and ranking
Lump Sum Funding: What Do I Need to Know?, version 3.0 · slide 10 · Evaluation of a lump sum proposal

cards.title: Conditional and exceptional requirements
cards.answer:
The storage topic adds ownership-control and satellite-data conditions.
- Conditional — China control: entities directly or indirectly controlled by China or Chinese entities cannot participate.
- Conditional — Satellite services: use Copernicus and/or Galileo/EGNOS when using relevant earth-observation or positioning services.
- Conditional — Sensitive information: security appraisal may impose grant conditions.
cards.sources:
Integrated Approaches for Retrofitting Infrastructures with Innovative Energy Storage Technologies · Topic conditions and documents, Other Eligible Conditions
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 16–17 · Security — EU classified and sensitive information
